title: LeBron James Signs With Philadelphia 76ers in Pursuit of Fifth Championship
excerpt: The NBA's all-time leading scorer agreed to a two-year, $8 million deal to join Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, forgoing bigger paydays for one last shot at a title.
body:
• LeBron James signed a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers, his smallest deal since entering the league as a rookie in 2003.
  • The 41-year-old joins Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and recently acquired Jaylen Brown on a Sixers team that has not won an NBA title since 1983.
  • James considered retirement after the Lakers were swept in the second round of the 2026 playoffs before choosing Philadelphia over the Heat, Cavaliers and Warriors.
  • The signing moved Philadelphia's championship odds from 20-1 to 10-1, making the Sixers instant Eastern Conference contenders.

LeBron James ended weeks of league-wide speculation on Friday, announcing he will join the Philadelphia 76ers for what he called the final chapter of his NBA career. The league's all-time leading scorer agreed to a two-year, $8 million contract with a player option, ESPN's Shams Charania reported, confirmed by Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul.

The deal represents a dramatic pay cut for James, who earned over $48 million with the Los Angeles Lakers last season. But at 41, entering a record-extending 24th NBA season, the four-time champion made clear that money was no longer the priority.

"This is my last decision. I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship."

— LeBron James, via social media

Why Philadelphia

James joins a 76ers roster that has been quietly rebuilt into one of the East's most talented lineups. He will play alongside center Joel Embiid, guard Tyrese Maxey — who earned his first All-NBA selection last season — and forward Jaylen Brown, acquired from the Boston Celtics in a blockbuster trade earlier this offseason.

https://x.com/ESPNNBA/status/2080742369649922460

According to ESPN, James did not seriously consider the 76ers until Philadelphia landed Brown. Once the Celtics star arrived, the Sixers' roster became the most attractive landing spot for a player singularly focused on winning a fifth ring. The presence of new general manager Mike Gansey, who worked alongside James during his second stint in Cleveland, helped seal the deal, according to Charania.

Philadelphia emerged from a crowded field of suitors. The Miami Heat, Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves all pursued James, who became a free agent after opting out of his Lakers contract in June.

From Near-Retirement to a New Beginning

James revealed that he came close to walking away from basketball entirely. The Lakers were swept by the eventual champion New York Knicks in the second round of the 2026 playoffs, and James said the loss left him questioning whether he had anything left to give.

"I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game."

— LeBron James

He averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists and 6.1 rebounds in 60 games last season, earning a league-record 22nd consecutive All-Star selection. In March, he surpassed Robert Parish's record for most career regular-season games played.

What It Means for the NBA

The signing immediately reshuffles the Eastern Conference hierarchy. The Sixers, who squeaked into the 2026 playoffs as the seventh seed before falling to the Knicks in the second round, jumped from 20-1 championship odds to 10-1 within hours of the announcement, according to Reuters.

Philadelphia has not won an NBA championship since 1983, when Julius Erving and Moses Malone swept the Lakers. For a franchise that has endured decades of near-misses and Process-era rebuilds, James represents perhaps the most consequential free-agent signing in team history.

James spent eight seasons with the Lakers, where he won the 2020 championship and became the NBA's all-time leading scorer. He leaves as the franchise's most productive player of the modern era, averaging 25.9 points, 7.9 assists and 7.7 rebounds across 479 regular-season games.

A Global Story

James's move will reverberate beyond North America. The NBA has been expanding aggressively in India, hosting preseason games and securing major streaming deals. LeBron remains the league's most recognizable global ambassador, and his presence on a competitive Eastern Conference team gives the NBA a compelling new narrative heading into the 2026-27 season. For the league's rapidly growing Indian fanbase, James's pursuit of a fifth title with a new team adds another chapter to the most storied career in modern basketball.
